title: Plug-and-Play Inference Pilot Playbook for Platform Engineers
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook is a plug-and-play guide for platform engineers and solutions teams running a short pilot of Redwood Inference. The document focuses on technical integration patterns, persuasive positioning and messaging for platform and product teams, competitive talking points, pragmatic pricing guidance for pilots, a compact case vignette, and a concise security FAQ for prospects. Use this as a field-ready checklist and messaging binder for pilots expected to run 4–8 weeks.

Audience
- Platform engineers and platform product managers evaluating inference runtimes
- Solutions engineers and account teams running proof-of-value pilots
- Sales and solution architects needing reproducible messaging for technical buyers

Quick summary
- Goal: Show measurable delta in latency, cost per 1M tokens, and operational complexity vs incumbent approach in 30 days
- Target success metrics: 2x improvement in p50 generation latency or 30% lower per-token cost while meeting quality targets
- Typical pilot scope: 1–2 model endpoints, 10k–100k tokens/day, 1–3 integration routes (sync stub, streaming chat, and embeddings)

Positioning & Messaging (Platform-focused)

Core positioning statements (short)
- Redwood Inference enables predictable inference economics with production-grade SLAs and a single API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- For platform teams, Redwood reduces operational ownership by providing a runtime with built-in batching, caching, and model variants while preserving full control over rollout policies.

Messaging cues for platform conversations
- Opener: 'We enable your product teams to standardize on a single inference API while reducing token spend and operational toil.'
- Economics: 'You can tune batching and cache policies per route to trade latency vs cost; typical customers see 20–50% unit cost reductions in month 1.'
- Reliability: 'Automatic fallback to compatible model variants keeps endpoints live during capacity events; target SLOs are 99.9% availability.'
- Compliance: 'Private deployment options with KMS/HSM integration and audit logs let you run in VPC or on-prem when required.'

Competitive brief (concise)

Competitors covered: general cloud AI endpoints (vendor A), simple LLM APIs (vendor B), self-hosted inference runtimes (open project C).

Differentiators to stress
- Unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private: reduces refactor cost when moving from POC to production.
- Cost controls: transparent token-level cost breakdowns and automated recommendations for quantization and batching.
- Operational guardrails: canary rollouts, automatic fallbacks, and built-in tracing for per-request latency breakdowns.

Weaknesses to acknowledge proactively
- For extremely experimental model research, Redwood is optimized for production serving rather than research workflows.
- On-prem lifts require coordination with our Private deployment team (2–4 week lead depending on customer environment).

Pilot architecture and technical checklist

Pilot objective examples
1) In-app chat latency optimization: baseline -> Redwood variant, measure p50/p95 and model cost per response.
2) Embeddings migration: compare embedding quality and per-vector cost across quantized models.
3) Reranking pipeline: end-to-end throughput and cost on re-ranking 10 candidates per query.

Required stakeholders
- Customer: platform engineer, security lead, product owner
- Redwood: solutions engineer (SE), deployment engineer, technical account rep (TAR)

Pilot flow (recommended 4–6 weeks)
1) Week 0: Scoping call, success metrics, and test dataset collection
2) Week 1: Sandbox access and sample integration, baseline capture (latency, cost, correctness)
3) Week 2: Tune batching, KV/prefix caching, and select quantization profile; run A/B tests versus baseline
4) Week 3: Observability and tracing walkthrough; adjust rollout policy; run load test to target 2x baseline traffic
5) Week 4: Business review, escalate to Dedicated or Private path if accepted; produce executive summary with metrics

Minimal technical configuration (example)
| Component | Recommended setting | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
|Latency SLO | p50 < 120 ms for short responses | Target depends on use case; chat can accept higher p50 but aim for p95 < 500 ms |
|Batch window | 5–20 ms | Start small to prioritize latency, increase for throughput testing |
|Cache TTL | 60–180s for repeated prompts | Use for assistant prefaces or template-heavy traffic |
|Quantization profile | int8 or q4_0 where acceptable | Validate quality with prompt set before rollouts |
|Autoscale policy | target CPU/GPU util 60–80% | Keep burst headroom during load tests |

Sample API integration snippets
- REST (sync generation):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"open-llm-q4", "input":"Summarize the following..."}'
```
- Streaming best practice: open a streaming endpoint and use continuous token flush to UI; enable prefix caching for repeated system prompts.

Pricing guidance and pilot sizing

Pilot pricing model (recommended for field teams)
- Offer a limited-time pilot credit (e.g., $5k–$25k depending on expected token volume) convertible into committed spend if customer converts within 60 days.
- Provide two pricing approaches for pilots: (A) usage-based with per-token tiered discounts, and (B) fixed pilot bundle (includes X tokens, 24/7 SE support for duration).

Sizing worksheet (example inputs)
- Expected daily active users (DAU): 5k
- Average tokens per session: 350
- Expected days of pilot: 30
- Token volume = DAU * tokens * days = 5k * 350 * 30 = 52.5M tokens

Suggested pilot offers based on volume
- Small ( <= 10M tokens): 30-day free sandbox + 2k pilot credit + basic SE support
- Medium (10–75M tokens): 30–45 day pilot credit $5k–$10k + 1 week dedicated SE + cost per token capped at pilot rate
- Large ( >75M tokens): bespoke credit and dedicated deployment planning; propose Dedicated capacity trial with SLA

Bill of success (metrics to capture during pilot)
- Latency p50/p95, error rate, average tokens per request, token cost per 1k responses, developer time to integrate (hours), uptime

Pitch deck outline & messaging cues (1-page speaker notes)

1) Problem slide: multi-model sprawl, unpredictable token costs, and brittle rollouts
2) Solution slide: Redwood single API, batching/caching, and unified rollout controls
3) Economic impact: show before/after token costs and TCO reduction estimate
4) Architecture slide: hosted/dedicated/private options and fallback routes
5) Pilot ask: clear pilot scope, expected metrics, and Redwood commitments (credits/SE time)

Case vignette (compact)

Customer: mid-market SaaS in customer support
Pilot scope: migrate inference for 3 chat flows and embeddings for intent classification
Results (30 days): p50 reduced from 240 ms to 110 ms; token cost down 38%; integration time 48 hours; one week to full A/B rollout.

Security FAQ for prospects (technical buyer primer)

Q: How is customer data protected in hosted mode?
A: Transport-level TLS, per-tenant isolation, configurable retention policies, and optional request-level PII redaction. Audit logs available via the Console or exported to SIEM.

Q: Do you support bring-your-own-key (BYOK)?
A: Yes. Private and Dedicated deployments integrate with KMS/HSM providers for key rotation and separation of duties.

Q: What data residency controls exist?
A: Region pinning is supported for hosted; Private deployments run in customer VPC for full data residency control.

Q: How do you handle vulnerability disclosures and patching?
A: We maintain an industry-standard disclosure process, quarterly runtime patches, and emergency CVE responses with targeted remediation windows.

Q: Can we get an architecture diagram for on-prem deployment?
A: Yes. Provide contact TAR for an environment intake checklist and a tailored reference architecture.

Operational ownership and escalation

- Field SE: initial integration, quality validation, pilot metrics
- TAR: post-pilot sizing and Dedicated/Private transition
- Platform owner (customer): maintains traffic routing and authentication configuration

Next steps (template for email to prospect)
1) Confirm pilot scope and success metrics (reply with dataset link)
2) Provide Sandbox access and invite 2 customer engineers to the Console
3) Schedule 90-minute kickoff and 30-minute mid-pilot health review
4) Agree conversion criteria and exec readout date
